purpose: Short historical screen of externally documented strategy concepts. Not validation; decides nothing about profitability.

window.note: 14 calendar days (10 trading days) of development data already used by Phases 5-5.2; not sealed, not forward.

costs: frozen Phase 5 cost model: market spread (configured 0.30 fallback), commission 3.50 USD/lot/side, slippage 0.05 USD

rules: INCONCLUSIVE if fewer than 15 M5 trades (or not screened for lack of an indicator).
REJECTED if M5 expectancy after costs <= 0, or the concept is unsuitable for GoldScalp's data or its own source shows it unprofitable.
WORTH FURTHER RESEARCH only if M5 expectancy > 0, PF >= 1.1, still positive without its best day, positive with costs x2, and M15 execution not negative.

candidates.name: London breakout of the Asian range

sources.title: London Breakout Strategy
sources.org: The Right Trader (educational, vendor of tools)

sources.title: London Breakout on Gold: 3.7 Years of Backtests

candidates.original_rules: M15. Range = high/low of 00:00-07:00 UTC; skip if range < 0.25x or > 0.80x daily ATR(14). Entry 07:00-10:00 UTC on the first M15 CLOSE beyond the range (earlier side wins). Stop: opposite side of the range. Target 1R. Exit at the first M15 close at or after 12:00 UTC. One trade per day.
candidates.evidence: FX source: none (says no reliable published win rate). Gold source: vendor backtest 2023-2026, PF 1.37-1.38 on ~715 trades, costs not stated, bull-market sample.
candidates.implementation: level_break of completed SESSION highs/lows on M15, known within 1 candle; London session with the New York overlap excluded (07:00-12:00 UTC in October); spread <= 0.50; structure stop beyond the last unbroken M15 swing (+0.1 ATR); 1R target; 300-minute time limit.
deviations: The engine's session levels are the most recent COMPLETED Asian (00:00-09:00 UTC), London and New York sessions, not a 00:00-07:00 range, so Asian levels exist only from 09:00 UTC and earlier breaks use the previous day's sessions.
Stop at the last M15 swing instead of the opposite side of the range (a range stop is not available).
No range-size filter; entries until 12:00 UTC instead of 10:00; not limited to one trade per day (one open position at a time).

candidates.name: Previous-day high/low false-breakout fade

sources.title: Intraday Strategies on Gold that Trade Against the Trend

candidates.original_rules: CME gold futures, M15: if price breaks below the previous day's low and comes back above it, go long; if it breaks above the previous day's high and crosses back below it, go short. Flat by the end of the day. Stop, target and filters not specified by the source.
candidates.evidence: Author-reported out-of-sample results since 2018 (average trades ~$135 and ~$100 net); not verifiable; the short side did poorly out of sample.
candidates.implementation: liquidity_sweep of the previous-day high/low (PD levels, previous trading day at the 17:00 New York rollover) on M15, confirmed within 1 candle; spread <= 0.50; structure stop beyond the last M15 swing (+0.1 ATR); no target; 360-minute time limit.
deviations: Stop and target are not specified by the source: a structure stop beyond the sweep swing and no target were used.
'Flat by the end of the day' approximated by a 6-hour holding limit.
Spot XAUUSD and the broker's previous day instead of CME futures.

candidates.name: EMA trend-pullback scalp

sources.title: Short-term momentum scalping in the forex market

candidates.original_rules: H1 trend: 8 EMA above 34 EMA and price above both (mirror for shorts). M5 entry after a pullback to/through the 8 EMA when trend-side momentum returns. Stop beyond the previous swing. Target not specified. No overnight holds.
candidates.evidence: None; the author says crossover systems have not worked well for him long-term.
candidates.implementation: ema_trend on H1 (9 vs 50 EMA, price and fast beyond slow); M5 swing_sequence 'pullback' (last low a higher low for longs) and a fresh M5 BOS in the trend direction within 2 candles; spread <= 0.50; structure stop beyond the last M5 swing (+0.1 ATR); 2R target; 240 minutes.
deviations: 8/34 EMAs are not available: the nearest available pair 9/50 was used.
'Pullback to the 8 EMA, then momentum returns' (discretionary) expressed as an M5 higher-low pullback followed by a fresh M5 break of structure.
Target not specified by the source: GoldScalp's standard 2R and 240-minute limit, for comparability with the baselines.

candidates.name: Crabel opening-range stretch breakout with NR4/NR7

sources.summary: book (Crabel 1990, not accessed) + research blog (Oxford Capital) + academic ORB on crude oil

candidates.not_screened_reason: Needs the session/day open, a 10-day stretch average and NR4/NR7 day ranges; no such levels exist in the builder. The documented version is a multi-day swing system on daily bars.

candidates.name: 5-minute opening-range breakout in the first candle's direction (Zarattini & Aziz)

sources.summary: academic working paper (SSRN 4416622) + independent replication (MQL5 blog, 2026)

candidates.not_screened_reason: Needs a first-N-minute opening range from a chosen anchor; not available. An independent replication on five indices found the gross edge disappears net of spread and slippage.

candidates.name: Noise-area intraday momentum (Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon)
candidates.not_screened_reason: Needs time-of-day volatility bands from the session open and half-hour checks; not available. SPY-only evidence.

candidates.name: First-half-hour to last-half-hour intraday momentum (Gao et al.)
candidates.not_screened_reason: Needs time-of-day returns and clock-time entries; not available. For GLD the predictive half-hour is not necessarily the first.

candidates.name: VWAP trend (Zarattini & Aziz)
candidates.not_screened_reason: Needs real traded volume to build VWAP; spot XAUUSD has only broker tick volume. Always-in-market flipping is extremely cost-sensitive. Unsuitable for GoldScalp's data.

candidates.name: Turtle Soup failed 20-bar breakout (Connors & Raschke)
candidates.not_screened_reason: Needs a 20-bar extreme at least 4 bars old; the nearest builder analogue (sweep of equal highs/lows or session levels) was already tested as VOL-F, R3 and R8, all rejected or not supported. No target in the source; daily-bar rules.

candidates.name: RSI(2) extreme mean reversion (Connors & Alvarez)
candidates.not_screened_reason: Needs RSI(2) at extremes (<= 5-10 / >= 90-95), a 200 SMA and a 5 SMA exit; the builder has RSI(14) confirmation only. No gold or intraday evidence; no stop in the original.

candidates.name: Bollinger %b mean reversion (Connors)
candidates.not_screened_reason: Needs Bollinger %b and a 200 SMA; not available. Academic evidence: Bollinger signals do not beat buy-and-hold after costs.

candidates.name: Bollinger / TTM squeeze breakout (Bollinger; Carter)
candidates.not_screened_reason: Needs Bollinger and Keltner bands and a momentum histogram; not available. The closest earlier analogue, R9 volatility-squeeze breakout, was rejected. No quantitative evidence.

candidates.name: 5-minute moving-average crossover on gold (Urquhart et al.)
candidates.not_screened_reason: Always-in-market crossover rules cannot be expressed (no crossover exit). The source's own evidence: standard parameters are not profitable even before costs; the best rules come from a 66,297-rule search (data-mining) with no costs. Not worth implementing.

candidates.name: Gold time-of-day and pre-London-fix short (Donati & Jung)
candidates.not_screened_reason: Needs clock-time entries and exits (11:00 and 02:00 New York); not available. The source's net-of-spread returns fell to about 1.7% a year in 2013-18 and the effect is decaying.
